sentences.text:
1 The submission of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that petitioners are the father-in-law,
mother-in-law, Nanad and Bua of the deceased, who is said to have died on 14.05.2024.
As per the allegations contained in the FIR in question it is alleged that applicants and other co-accused were harassing the deceased for demand of dowry.
It is further stated in the FIR that the petitioners who were instrumental in persuading the deceased to take extreme steps, which led to her death on 14.05.2024.
Having considering the material on record including the postmortem of the deceased, the deceased died in the house of husband.

The nature of ante-mortem injuries which have been placed does not persuade us to entertain the present writ petition, as it cannot be said that no cognizable offence is made out and whether the petitioner is involved therein or not can be seen during investigation.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, we decline to entertain the present writ petition,
leaving it open for the petitioners to take legal recourse, as is admissible under law.
With these observations, the petition is dismissed without prejudice to the rights of the petitioner in the pending investigation and also to pursue other remedies.
